items.title: Japanese court says voice is protected by publicity rights; US appeals court says AI training is not fair use
items.summary: There have been two judgments this week of relevance to the ongoing AI debates in the music industry. A Japanese court ruled that publicity rights allow performers to stop unapproved AI voice clones. Meanwhile a US appeals court ruled against an AI company that used the good old fair use defence

items.summary: Many of the music industry’s AI legal battles swing on whether or not AI training is ‘fair use’ under US copyright law. Donald Trump’s DoJ recently intervened in a dispute between newspapers and OpenAI insisting AI training is fair use. The newspapers have responded, explaining why the DoJ is wrong

tip.title: Registra antes de publicar, no después
tip.body: El registro de tu obra no crea el derecho de autor —ese nace con la creación— pero sí te da la prueba con fecha cierta que vale en un juicio. Regístrala antes de subirla a plataformas, no cuando ya tengas el problema.

tip.title: Register before you release, not after
tip.body: Registration doesn't create your copyright —that exists from the moment of creation— but it gives you dated proof that holds up in court. Register before uploading to platforms, not after trouble shows up.
